case_title: State of N.C.T. of Delhi v. Ajay Kumar Tyagi
accused_occupation: Junior Engineer with the Delhi Jal Board
neutral_facts: The accused, who was working as a Junior Engineer with the Delhi Jal Board, was involved in a case where a Constable applied for a water connection in the name of his wife. The accused was alleged to have demanded a bribe of Rs. 1000/- for clearing the file. A trap was laid, and the accused was alleged to have accepted the bribe. The charge-sheet was submitted, and the accused was put on trial. A departmental proceeding was also initiated against the accused, where the enquiry officer found that the evidence did not substantiate the charge of bribe-taking. The disciplinary authority exonerated the accused, but the High Court quashed the criminal proceedings on the premise that the accused had been exonerated in the departmental proceeding. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, stating that the exoneration in the departmental proceeding does not automatically lead to the quashing of the criminal prosecution. The accused was ordered to appear before the trial court for further proceedings.
